title: Formal proofs, mathematical claims, and what remains open
scope: This file defines how this repository distinguishes formal proof, intended mathematical meaning, public claims, and remaining open propositions. It does not prove any mathematical statement. Named LLM semantic review is the normal best-attempt authoring path; optional human or specialist review is recorded separately and may contest or upgrade that work later.
human_preamble: This page records the rules used to relate the Lean development to the mathematical claims made in this repository, and to keep partial results from being overstated. It is generated from `docs/methodology.json`; run `python3 scripts/build_methodology.py` after changing that source. Lean source checked by the pinned Lean kernel remains proof authority.
The machine source calls the six standing rules `method_axiom` records. They are repository rules, not Lean `axiom` declarations.

lean_check.decides: Whether the declaration elaborates and its proof term is accepted in the pinned environment. The associated axiom audit reports the transitive axioms the declaration depends on.
lean_check.does_not_decide: Whether the proposition expresses the intended mathematics, is relevant to an open problem, or is novel.

repository_check.decides: Whether identifiers, statuses, source coordinates, routes, projections, and generated files agree.
repository_check.does_not_decide: Whether an informal statement is mathematically faithful or significant.

named_semantic_review.decides: A named model's source-bound best attempt at the intended meaning of a formal proposition, its family placement, its significance and editorial rank, the public claim it supports, what remains open, and faithful exposition.
named_semantic_review.does_not_decide: Whether the Lean kernel accepts the proof term; whether novelty, priority, external peer review, or community acceptance has been established.

human_specialist_review.decides_label: Records a named reviewer's judgement about
human_specialist_review.decides: A contest, correction, confirmation, or upgrade of intended meaning, family placement, significance, editorial rank, exposition, or relation to prior work.
human_specialist_review.does_not_decide: Whether the Lean kernel accepts the proof term; nor does one review by itself establish novelty, priority, external peer-review consensus, or community acceptance.

blinded_recovery_evaluation.decides: Whether the layers present at a past revision expose the obligation a stated target requires, and whether a candidate offered against that revision is accepted by the Lean kernel in the environment of that revision. This is interpretation evidence about the layers as they stood. The holdout is a git checkout predating the target, so the target declaration is absent from the working tree by construction rather than by the agent's restraint.
blinded_recovery_evaluation.does_not_decide: Whether the derived layers shortened the work of producing the later result. A past checkout does not isolate acceleration, because a shared object store, later receipts and dossiers, network access, context supplied in the request, and a model's familiarity with public mathematics can each carry the answer into the run. It also does not decide whether the recovered statement is novel, significant, or correctly proved; whether the mechanism credited for the recovery is the one the original proof used; or whether a recovery generalises beyond the held-out case.

historical_layer_experiment.title: What a historical checkout can and cannot show

questions.statement: Given a stated target and a named candidate declaration, does the runtime at the parent revision expose the exact remaining obligation, and does the pinned kernel accept an authored candidate that carries neither the later declaration name nor the later module name, inside the constructed hybrid-dependency environment?
questions.note: This is a property of the runtime and of one authored candidate. It is a mechanical fixture result. No reader and no agent is observed, and no route is compared.

questions.statement: Do the semantic layers present at a revision let a reader find the relevant mathematics and interpret it correctly?
questions.research_question_association: scripts/historical_bridge_experiment.py is the harness the Q1 study would be built from. The association is a research-agenda link and is not a result.
why_the_current_run_does_not_answer_it: the candidate proof is authored in the harness rather than produced by a participant
the compiler request names the target statement and the exact candidate declaration, so the obligation is confirmed against an answer key rather than found
only the derived-layer arm is run, so no route is compared
no reader and no agent is in the loop, so interpretation is not observed at all
questions.what_would_answer_it: the fresh-context use experiment: two arms, the same task, target, permissions and budget, participants with no access to any wave report, audit or integration trace, and returns scored against the six outcomes of controlled_comparison

questions.statement: Do the historical derived layers shorten the work of producing a later result?
questions.note: A past checkout alone does not isolate acceleration. Every channel in leakage_channels with controlled false can carry the later answer into the run.

leakage_channels.channel: The checkout could silently be a different revision.
The later declaration name could appear in the past tree.
The later module file could exist in the past checkout.
The candidate source could name the later declaration or module.
The candidate could close its goal with sorry or admit.
Building more than the pre-existing dependency target could pull later source in.
The compiler could read the current tree instead of the past checkout.
Later-reuse evidence could be read before the proof run and steer it.
The disposable clone is made with git clone --shared, so every later commit, tree and blob of the current repository stays reachable by object id from inside the historical checkout.
leakage_channels.consequence: Report as a limitation until the clone is made without shared alternates.

leakage_channels.channel: The historical clone symlinks .lake/packages from the current tree, so it builds against the current dependency pin rather than the one the past revision declared.
leakage_channels.consequence: Report as a limitation; the environment is not the historical environment.

leakage_channels.channel: Only the later declaration name is screened. A paraphrase, a semantic node, a receipt, a dossier, or a prose statement at the past revision that describes the same bridge is not detected.
leakage_channels.consequence: Report as a limitation; name absence is weaker than content absence.

leakage_channels.channel: The request handed to the compiler already names the target statement and the exact candidate declaration.
leakage_channels.consequence: Obstruction recovery is conditioned on an answer key and must not be described as search.

leakage_channels.channel: The candidate proof is an authored reconstruction written with knowledge of the later proof.
leakage_channels.consequence: No synthesis claim may be made from this run.

leakage_channels.channel: No model runs inside the harness, so no search behaviour is observed.
leakage_channels.consequence: Nothing here measures what a model would find without the layers.

leakage_channels.channel: A model asked to reproduce a bridge on a public problem may have seen the mathematics during training.
leakage_channels.consequence: Report as a limitation of any later model-in-the-loop run.

leakage_channels.channel: Child processes are environment-sanitised and are not sandboxed against network or filesystem access.
leakage_channels.consequence: Report as a limitation until the runner isolates both.

leakage_channels.channel: Only the derived-layer arm is run, so no route comparison exists.
leakage_channels.consequence: No acceleration statement may be made from a single arm.

measured_outcomes.definition: The returned statement is logically equivalent to the target declaration's statement, with the same hypotheses and quantifiers.
The returned statement drops a hypothesis, widens a quantifier, or otherwise claims more than the target.
The returned statement omits a hypothesis the proof actually uses.
The run names the exact proposition that remains open after its contribution.
The returned artifact is accepted again from its stored bytes in the stated environment.
A maintainer can integrate the return without reconstructing the reasoning that produced it.

controlled_comparison.reporting_rule: Report both arms and every uncontrolled channel. A single-arm run with an authored candidate and a named candidate declaration reports Q0 only. It reports nothing about Q1 and nothing about Q2.

fixture_separation.development_fixture_rule: The half-divisor coefficient bridge was inspected while the harness was written. It may be used to debug the harness and must never be reported as an evaluation result.
fixture_separation.evaluation_case_rule: An evaluation case must be a target whose statement, proof, and derived-layer neighbourhood were not read while building or tuning the harness.

held_out_variant_classes.description: A result proved in a note by ordinary mathematics is described as Lean-checked, or a kernel-checked ingredient is presented as proving the endpoint.
held_out_variant_classes.checks: The run must return the correct evidence class for the target.

held_out_variant_classes.description: A strong claim exists in the source but a selector omits it, for example a headline flag left unset because no reviewed semantic node exists for it.
held_out_variant_classes.checks: The run must find the claim through a route other than the selector, or report the omission.

held_out_variant_classes.description: A module is present in every tree while one copy carries declarations the others lack.
held_out_variant_classes.checks: The run must detect that the same path holds different declaration sets.

held_out_variant_classes.description: A rendered document is out of step with its source, for example a root PDF and a paper-directory PDF that differ.
held_out_variant_classes.checks: The run must prefer the source of record and report the divergence.

held_out_variant_classes.description: A route is recorded as closed, and the obstruction that would close it has not itself been proved.
held_out_variant_classes.checks: The run must report the route as open and name the missing obstruction.

historical_layer_experiment.scope_limit: This design records how a historical run must be read. It proves nothing, and it licenses neither an interpretation claim nor an acceleration claim. The current run establishes obligation extraction and candidate admissibility in a constructed hybrid-dependency environment, and nothing beyond that.

environment_record.statement: The run does not reproduce the historical build environment. scripts/historical_bridge_experiment.py checks out the parent revision into a disposable clone and then symlinks .lake/packages from the current tree, so the parent source is elaborated against the current dependency set. The environment is a hybrid of past source and present dependencies, and the receipt must name it rather than leave it assumed.

required_receipt_fields.historical_build_receipt.declared_depend: the pins the parent revision declares, read at run time from git show <parent_commit>:lake-manifest.json and git show <parent_commit>:lean-toolchain
required_receipt_fields.historical_build_receipt.effective_depen: the pins the build actually uses, read from the current tree's lake-manifest.json and lean-toolchain, because .lake/packages is a symlink into the current tree
required_receipt_fields.historical_build_receipt.dependency_pin_: one of historical, current, or hybrid; the current design always produces hybrid
the package names whose revision differs between the two pin sets, together with the toolchain comparison; an empty list is a recorded finding and not an absent field

effective_pins_observed_in_the_release_c.source: lake-manifest.json and lean-toolchain at the release candidate root, read directly
effective_pins_observed_in_the_release_c.declared_pins_at_the_parent_revision: not transcribed here; reading them requires git in the release candidate, which the wave contract reserves for the conductor. The run must read them and record them.

environment_record.consequence: A verdict from this harness is a statement about the hybrid environment. It is not a statement about what the parent revision would have built on its own dependencies.

receipt_path_rule.writer: scripts/historical_bridge_experiment.py prints one JSON packet to standard output and writes no file. The runner captures that output to the staging path.
receipt_path_rule.promotion_rule: The staging file is promoted to the authoritative path only after every promotion condition holds. A partial, truncated or aborted output must never occupy the authoritative path, because a reader who finds a file there treats it as a completed run.
promotion_conditions: the staging file parses as JSON
experiment_design is present and carries question_answered
historical_build_receipt carries the four dependency pin fields of environment_record.required_receipt_fields
the process exit status is recorded in run_exit_status

values.complete: the run finished, every promotion condition held, and the verdict fields are all present
values.aborted: the run raised on a control check, for example a changed parent identity, a future module found in the parent checkout, or a failed historical dependency build; the reason is recorded in abort_reason
values.partial: the run stopped without an abort reason, for example on a budget timeout or an interrupted build

companion_fields.run_exit_status: the process exit status of the run

status_field_contract.reader_rule: A receipt whose status is not complete carries no verdict and supports no sentence in any paper, README or claim record. Only the authoritative path is citable, and only at status complete.

human_capsule: The exact boundary between proved and open must remain explicit.
Lean checks the stated proposition; it does not check that the proposition expresses the intended mathematics.
A public claim is transferred between representations only through a proved implication or equivalence.
A reduction must state the hypothesis or quantifier that remains open.
A finite result remains finite unless a theorem supplies the unbounded or universal step.
Progress toward an open problem must state which outstanding obligation it proves, narrows, decomposes, re-expresses, or constrains.

mathematical_objects.definition: An unresolved mathematical proposition whose status matters to this programme; in the claim registry these are the claims with status open.
Coordinates, an encoding, a recurrence, a series identity, or another model in which a target is studied.
A proposition proved from a hypothetical assumption such as rationality or the existence of a counterexample.
A checked implication or equivalence that transfers a mathematical obligation in a stated direction.
Finite data accepted by a proved checker as establishing a bounded proposition.
The exact unresolved proposition left after the proved work.

repository_objects.definition: A named Lean object in the pinned checked environment.
A public mathematical statement with a status, intended meaning, and links to any supporting Lean declarations.
A human-facing or machine-facing view derived from formal source, public claims, or this methodology source.

method_axioms.title: Proof means the exact proposition checked by Lean
method_axioms.human_name: A formal result is the exact proposition Lean checked
method_axioms.statement: A result is proved here only as the exact elaborated proposition accepted by the pinned public Lean environment under its transitive assumptions.
method_axioms.scope_limit: Kernel acceptance does not establish intended meaning, relevance, novelty, or claim status.

method_axioms.title: Formal proof does not verify intended meaning
method_axioms.human_name: Formal validity and mathematical faithfulness are separate questions
method_axioms.statement: A checked Lean declaration and its intended mathematical statement remain distinct until a named semantic review records a source-bound best-attempt correspondence.
method_axioms.scope_limit: Semantic review does not become proof authority. Optional human or specialist review may contest, correct, confirm, or upgrade the recorded judgement later.

method_axioms.title: Representation changes require a proved implication or equivalence
method_axioms.human_name: A public claim crosses representations only through proved transport
method_axioms.statement: A claim may move between coordinates, encodings, normalisations, or models only through a checked implication or equivalence whose direction and losses are explicit.
method_axioms.scope_limit: A transport theorem establishes the stated relation; it does not establish that the new representation is useful.

method_axioms.title: A reduction states the remaining open hypothesis
method_axioms.human_name: A reduction keeps the remaining hypothesis visible
method_axioms.statement: Every conditional theorem, criterion, or reduction names the exact hypothesis or quantifier that remains open.
method_axioms.scope_limit: An exact reduction can expose an open proposition without proving it.

method_axioms.title: A finite result remains finite without an unbounded or universal theorem
method_axioms.human_name: Finite verification does not change quantifiers
method_axioms.statement: Finite certificates, bounded searches, and verified initial segments remain finite evidence unless a checked theorem supplies the unbounded or universal step.
method_axioms.scope_limit: Increasing a checked bound does not change the quantifier of the public claim.

method_axioms.title: Progress toward an open problem names the outstanding obligation it affects
method_axioms.human_name: A claim of progress names both the theorem and the outstanding obligation
method_axioms.statement: A result advances an open target only when it states which remaining open proposition it proves, narrows, decomposes, re-expresses, or constrains.
method_axioms.scope_limit: The repository checks that the effect is explicit; named semantic review supplies the best-attempt significance judgement, without asserting external peer review, novelty, priority, or community acceptance.

principles.title: State a partial result and the remaining open proposition together
principles.statement: Every frontier-facing partial result states both its positive conclusion and the exact proposition that survives it.
principles.scope_limit: Closed results that do not face an open target need not invent a remaining-open field.

principles.title: Derive exact consequences from a hypothetical assumption
principles.statement: Under a hypothetical rational value or counterexample, derive checked structural consequences instead of replacing proof with plausibility.
principles.scope_limit: This is a method for developing consequences, not a claim that every useful proof must use contradiction.

principles.title: Calling a finite checker exact requires soundness and completeness
principles.statement: A finite checker needs a soundness theorem; calling it exact additionally requires a completeness theorem at the stated parameters.
principles.scope_limit: Soundness and completeness at fixed parameters do not provide an unbounded supply of certificates.

principles.title: Record what a representation change preserves, reflects, or loses
principles.statement: Each representation change identifies the checked theorem that transfers the claim and states the direction and any loss.
principles.scope_limit: Informal similarity between two representations is not a transfer theorem.

principles.title: Record failed routes and counterexamples when they constrain later work
principles.statement: A failed strategy, counterexample, or disproved finite-state interpretation is retained when it rules out a recurring mathematical route.
principles.scope_limit: Routine failed experiments and private working notes are not automatically public artefacts.

principles.title: Classify a change before updating public claims
principles.statement: Distinguish proof-body, proposition, assumption, representation, finite-range, claim-status, exposition, and projection changes before deciding what must be updated.
principles.scope_limit: The classification routes review; it does not decide the review outcome.

principles.title: Separate Lean, named semantic, and specialist authority
principles.statement: Lean owns formal validity. A named LLM best attempt is the normal author for intended meaning, family placement, significance and editorial ranking, and exposition. Optional human or specialist review is a separate record that may contest or upgrade that work; it is not a prerequisite for publishing an honest bounded result.
principles.scope_limit: Neither LLM semantic review nor human or specialist review proves a Lean proposition. Named semantic review does not establish novelty, priority, external peer review, or community acceptance.

principles.title: Update authoritative sources before projections
principles.statement: Update Lean source first, then checked assumptions and named semantic review, then claim status, authored exposition, and generated projections. Record any later human or specialist review alongside the semantic record rather than turning it into a publication gate.
principles.scope_limit: A proof-body-only change does not automatically authorize stronger prose.

principles.title: A public checkout must explain the claims and open boundary
principles.statement: A reader using only the public checkout must be able to find the main argument, proof routes, public claim statuses, and remaining open propositions.
principles.scope_limit: Path and projection checks establish availability, not reader comprehension.

principles.title: Claim assurance checks underclaiming as well as overclaiming
principles.statement: Public claim review checks both ceilings and coverage: prose must not exceed the checked theorem chain, and a source-backed high-value mechanism, exact reformulation, quantitative reduction, or distinct endpoint must be mechanically discoverable when omitting it would materially understate the corpus.
principles.scope_limit: Coverage does not turn support lemmas into separate headline claims: group plumbing under the smallest faithful contribution and record the named semantic significance judgement and its uncertainty.

anti_principles.title: Do not equate Lean acceptance with intended meaning
anti_principles.statement: Do not use a successful Lean check to bypass review of whether the proposition expresses the intended mathematics.
anti_principles.scope_limit: The repository requires a named, source-bound semantic judgement before claim publication; the normal authoring path is an LLM best attempt, not an automatic promotion rule or a mandatory human gate.

anti_principles.title: Do not report a reduction as a solution
anti_principles.statement: Do not narrate a conditional implication, equivalence, or criterion as closure of the original open problem.
anti_principles.scope_limit: An exact and useful reduction remains a genuine result when its remaining hypothesis is explicit.

anti_principles.title: Do not generalize a finite result without a theorem
anti_principles.statement: Do not treat a large checked range as evidence for an unbounded or universal assertion.
anti_principles.scope_limit: Finite results may be valuable without changing the universal claim.

anti_principles.title: Do not identify two representations without proved transport
anti_principles.statement: Do not speak of a transformed representation as the original claim unless a checked implication or equivalence supplies that relation.
anti_principles.scope_limit: This rule concerns claim transfer, not the informal use of notation.

anti_principles.title: Do not treat a graph, model output, or private work as proof authority
anti_principles.statement: A dependency graph, generated explanation, language-model output, or private proof sketch is not public proof authority.
anti_principles.scope_limit: These artefacts may help navigation or discovery without becoming proof.

anti_principles.title: Do not use output volume as mathematical progress
anti_principles.statement: Counts of declarations, proof lines, certificates, or agent activity do not by themselves establish progress on an open problem.
anti_principles.scope_limit: Scale metrics may describe the artefact; they do not change a mathematical claim.

anti_principles.title: Do not edit a projection as though it were the source
anti_principles.statement: README, generated Markdown, the corpus descriptor, and declaration maps must remain below their owning source files.
anti_principles.scope_limit: The paper is authored exposition and is checked for bounded agreement rather than generated from this file.

anti_principles.title: Do not keep a rule without an owner, a check or review route, and a scope limit
anti_principles.statement: A methodology rule is removed if it cannot name the objects or changes it applies to, the evidence it requires, the route that evaluates it, and what it does not establish.
anti_principles.scope_limit: A named semantic-review route is valid when the judgement is not machine-decidable; its model or reviewer identity, source, scope, judgement, and uncertainties must still be explicit.

worked_examples.title: An exact reduction that does not close #249
route: a hypothetical rational value of S = ∑ φ(n)/2ⁿ
an integrality constraint on totient tail differences
a finite non-integrality certificate at fixed parameters (certifiedKill)
the unbounded supply of such certificates, which remains open
worked_examples.narrative: If S were rational, its totient tails would satisfy an integrality constraint. The certifiedKill predicate refutes that constraint at fixed parameters, and the completeness theorem shows the finite computation loses no information at those parameters. The reduction theorem then proves: if certificates occur at unbounded parameters, S is irrational. Producing that unbounded supply is the remaining open proposition; nothing in this repository claims it.

worked_examples.title: Finite verification that stays finite
worked_examples.narrative: certifiedKill_all_small and the lcm-diagonal deposits through t = 8 (certifiedKill_periodLcm_diagonal_upto_six and the t = 7 and t = 8 endpoints) are kernel-checked with decide at fixed bounds. Each names a specific bounded region the checker has cleared; together with the generated certificate shards they show the reduction is not vacuous. The claim keeps the status verified finite instance and states its bounded domain. Raising the checked bound changes the stated bound; it does not change the quantifier of any public claim.

worked_examples.title: Necessary structure that does not yet contradict
worked_examples.narrative: The carry and zero-window theorems state what a rational series value would force: reciprocal-mass lower bounds, unbounded carry states, and sublogarithmic zero windows in divisor coverage. These are necessary consequences of rationality. They constrain a hypothetical rational value; none of them rules it out, and the universal #257 statement remains open.

semantic_review_triggers.description: The wording of a public claim changes.
The status of a public claim changes.
The reviewed correspondence between a proposition and its intended statement changes.
What the repository says a result means for an open problem changes.
The meaning of a methodology rule changes, not only its wording or projection.

forbidden_effect_vocabulary.description: The change must not alter the status of an open target claim.
The change must not derive an unbounded or universal statement from bounded evidence.
The change must not strengthen the wording of any public claim.
The change must not present a transformed representation as the original claim without a checked transport theorem.
The change must not edit a generated projection except by regenerating it from its owner.

change_classes.summary: A proof body changes; the stated proposition does not
change_classes.public_consequence: No claim or exposition change follows automatically. Compare the axiom audit before and after.

change_classes.summary: A stated proposition or its hypotheses change
change_classes.public_consequence: Reconcile the claim wording, the remaining-open boundary, and the paper statement.

change_classes.summary: The transitive assumptions of a declaration change
change_classes.public_consequence: Reassess the proof posture even when the proposition is unchanged.

change_classes.summary: A claim moves between coordinates, encodings, or models
change_classes.public_consequence: Record the transport theorem, its direction, and anything not preserved.

change_classes.summary: A checked bounded range or certificate family is extended
change_classes.public_consequence: Keep the finite status; update only the stated bound.

change_classes.summary: A claim's declaration coordinates or links are corrected; the claim is otherwise unchanged
change_classes.public_consequence: Link or correct the supporting declarations of an unchanged claim, then regenerate dependent projections. The mathematical claim does not change; a Lean check confirms the linked declaration exists and elaborates.

change_classes.summary: An advances-open-target relation is added or changed
change_classes.public_consequence: Record the outstanding obligation affected and the exact relation.

change_classes.summary: The status of a public claim changes
change_classes.public_consequence: State the theorem or review that licenses the new status.

change_classes.summary: Authored paper or documentation prose changes mathematically
change_classes.public_consequence: Prose must not exceed the status recorded in the claim registry.
Regenerate below the existing owners; no mathematical effect.
Regenerate METHODOLOGY.md and the corpus descriptor. Rules route review; they do not decide mathematics.

transition_contracts.title: From a Lean declaration to a public claim
transition_contracts.trigger: A new declaration or a changed proposition is proposed as support for a public claim.
requirements: The declaration exists in the pinned public source and passes the Lean check.
The public claim links to the declaration and uses a declared claim status.
A named, source-bound semantic review records the best-attempt judgement that the proposition expresses the intended paper-facing statement.
Any remaining open proposition is stated explicitly.

transition_contracts.title: From a changed representation to a public claim
transition_contracts.trigger: A claim is moved into different coordinates, an encoding, a recurrence, or another model.
requirements: A checked implication or equivalence identifies the direction of transfer.
The claim states anything not preserved by the transfer.
A named, source-bound semantic review records the best-attempt judgement that the transferred statement is the intended one.

transition_contracts.title: From a conditional reduction to a public claim
transition_contracts.trigger: A checked implication or equivalence is published with status conditional reduction.
requirements: The supporting declaration is linked.
The claim names at least one remaining open proposition from docs/claims.json.
The public statement says what the reduction does not prove.

transition_contracts.title: From a finite certificate to a public claim
transition_contracts.trigger: A checked finite computation or bounded family is added as a new public claim, or its interpretation changes.
requirements: The claim status remains verified finite instance.
The checked finite domain is explicit.
No open target changes status without a separate unbounded or universal theorem.

A purely mechanical extension of an already reviewed bounded family follows the finite_certificate_range_changed change class instead: Lean and repository checks, with review re-entered only when claim text, claim status, intended meaning, or the paper statement changes.

transition_contracts.title: From a public claim to an advances-open-target edge
transition_contracts.trigger: The argument graph says that a public claim advances an open target.
requirements: The target claim has status open.
The edge names a remaining open proposition owned by that target.
The edge states whether the result proves, narrows, decomposes, re-expresses, or constrains that proposition.

transition_contracts.title: From methodology source to public projections
requirements: METHODOLOGY.md is regenerated exactly from docs/methodology.json.
The corpus descriptor records the methodology path, schema, digest, and compact capsule.
AGENTS.md and README.md route to the methodology without duplicating its full content.
README.md carries no methodology machine identifiers beyond the source link.

validation_guards.description: Checks the methodology schema, literal object and change references, evidence classes, rule fields, local-instance references, change-class evidence and review requirements, guard references, and reciprocal guard-to-rule bindings.
Checks typed remaining-open propositions, conditional reductions, finite claim domains, and advances-open-target edge effects.
Checks that METHODOLOGY.md is the exact deterministic projection of docs/methodology.json.
Checks that the claim-map entrypoint, corpus descriptor, AGENTS.md, and README.md route to the methodology source and human projection, and that README carries no methodology machine identifiers.
Checks that public Lean source contains no sorry, admit, native_decide, or added axiom declarations.
